INVALID_VERIFICATION.definition: The verification transaction is not valid enough to produce a scientific preservation judgment.
triggers: broken or missing provenance for critical source evidence
corrupt or structurally invalid assertion graph
claim-bearing source text with critical extraction coverage failure
critical unresolved source coreference/context needed to define the proposition
missing required protected container or evidence dependency
INVALID_VERIFICATION.meaning: No judgment that the candidate is scientifically wrong.

REJECT.definition: A material scientific change is supported by traceable evidence in an otherwise valid verification transaction.
triggers: critical scope expansion/restriction not licensed by source

REVIEW.definition: The transaction is valid, but material uncertainty prevents automatic PASS and evidence is insufficient for REJECT.
triggers: multiple plausible alignments with materially different meaning
plausible new information whose source support cannot be established
uncertain split/merge preservation affecting a critical assertion

PASS_CANDIDATE.definition: Meaning is preserved relative to the source and verified scope; this is not a claim of external scientific truth.
requirements: all critical source-to-candidate alignments are preserved
all critical candidate-to-source alignments are supported
every critical decision dependency has a minimal traceable evidence path

non_compensation: Many correct relations cannot compensate for one critical wrong relation.
Similarity, NLI, embedding, model agreement, or aggregate score cannot override a critical deterministic failure.
A high acceptance score cannot compensate for any observed dangerous escape in a safety gate.
